thread:
emma: Customer on private VPC reporting intermittent 429s and backend timeouts during their morning batch window. They say their gateway (customer-managed Envoy) accepts a 1s burst then drops a lot of connections. Logs attached.
mike: Sorry about that — can you drop the ingress config and any rate-limiter settings they have? Also their observed QPS and usual concurrency numbers.
emma: They sent this ingress snippet (redacted):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: customer-api
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "10"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm: "600"
  spec: ...
```
They also run an external rate-limit service with per-customer token buckets (redis). Observed burst: ~300rps for ~6s, then 429s for ~30s. Customer expects short bursts allowed up to 500 then smoothing.
sam: :eyes: The `limit-connections` + external token bucket can interact poorly if connection drains are synchronous. Nginx/Envoy will queue then quickly fail if the token bucket refills slower than connection churn. What GKE node sizes and pod replicas are they on?
emma: 3 replicas, 4vCPU pods, nodepool autoscaling disabled. Client side does 8 concurrent connections per worker, 50 workers.
maria: Quick checklist: 1) confirm the external rate-limit TTL/atomic increments (race if multiple proxies) 2) check ingress controller burst/window config (nginx/Envoy have different defaults) 3) avoid identical per-route hard caps at proxy + service level. Suggest short-term relaxing of proxy-side hard caps and rely on token bucket service for smoothing.
infra-bot: [alert] rate-limit-service: redis-latency-spike detected at 1977000012 (p50 60ms -> 1.2s)

sam: For Envoy use-case, try setting a larger local token cache and a smoothing window. Example envoy filter snippet to allow short bursts and smooth over 15s: 
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
    stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 600
      tokens_per_fill: 40
      fill_interval: 2s
```
That gives ~600 token buffer with fills to avoid immediate 429s when redis flaps.
emma: Great. Customer also asked about k8s ingress annotation alternative since they're on nginx. Any nginx examples?
sam: For nginx ingress controller you can use the lua-based smoothing or adjust `limit_conn` + `limit_req` with burst and `nodelay` off. Eg:
```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=100r/s;
server {
  location / {
    limit_req zone=one burst=400 nodelay; # consider removing nodelay => smoother queuing
  }
}
```
Setting `burst` > expected short spikes and removing `nodelay` lets requests queue briefly rather than immediate 429s.
mike: Note: raising burst/queues can increase P99 latency and have billing/timeout side effects upstream. Ask customer to increase upstream timeouts for the batch window (temporarily) and monitor error budget.
jordan: We tried increasing burst to 400 but still saw a tail of 429s. Our redis token service had a failover hiccup during the spike. Any fallback suggestions?
emma: We recommended enabling a small local token cache in front of redis and fallback to permissive mode for <5s windows while alerting. Also increase readiness probe tolerances so pods don't mark unhealthy on short bursts.
maria: Operational playbook: 1) short-term: increase ingress burst and add local token cache; 2) mid-term: enable node autoscaling to handle sustained peaks; 3) long-term: move per-customer throttles to a hierarchical quota (per-route bucket + per-account bucket) and implement a leaky smoothing worker on the client side.
sam: Repro steps (customer provided) — run this script to reproduce the burst pattern: 
```bash
# spawn 50 workers each firing 6 reqs/sec for 10s
for i in $(seq 1 50); do 
  (for j in $(seq 1 60); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://api.customer.internal/endpoint & done; wait) &
done; wait
```
This should trigger the 6s spike then show 429s if smoothing not in place.
emma: I'll send the envoy/local-ratelimit patch to the customer and propose trial window for tomorrow morning. I'll attach logs and the repro script. :thumbsup:
mike: Thanks, team — escalate to private-deploy-specialist if customer needs us to modify their VPC proxies. Marking as support ticket #CS-7142 and tracking rollback plan.
